language.title: Language
language.help: The language used for the app UI and for the characters. Text the AI newly writes — diaries, award speeches — follows this too (already-written text stays as it is).

general.summarizerHelp: Summarizes the task label above each head with the chosen summarizer. Uses that account's quota (or API credits).
general.diaryHelp: Each character writes a work log / diary in their own voice at the end of every session (the manual ‘Write diary’ button still works). It calls the same CLI as the summarizer above, so it uses account quota. Read it from the tab's right-click menu.
general.observerHelp: Alerts and timing for Claude, Codex, Pi, Kilo and Antigravity apply to terminals created from now on. When off, the exclamation alert and session timing do not work.
general.openrouterNote: OpenRouter summaries use an API key (or the OPENROUTER_API_KEY variable). Without a key the summary fails and the raw text is shown.
general.opencodeNote: opencode summaries call the installed opencode CLI. Model ids use provider/model form (see opencode models), and the default assumes opencode's own plan (opencode-go).
general.commandHelp: Command to run for summaries. Leave empty to run {{command}}. You can point this at a wrapper script for a separate account, or at an absolute path — one program only, no arguments.
general.lightModelHelp: Model used for task labels and character diaries. Leave empty for the default ({{model}}).
general.heavyModelHelp: Model used for long texts such as session-log study notes. Leave empty for the default ({{model}}).
general.openrouterKeyHelp: Once saved it stays in the app and is never shown again.
general.anthropicKeyHelp: Used to load the Claude model list (or the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY variable). Once saved it stays in the app and is never shown again.
general.summaryTestInstruction: Summarize the following text in one sentence.
general.summaryTestText: This is a test sentence sent from the settings screen to check that the summarizer actually answers. If a summary comes back, both the command and the light model are set correctly.
general.errorSummarizerDisabled: Summaries are turned off (turn them on in the General tab)
general.errorCommandNotFound: Command not found (check that it is installed and that the command field is right)

sound.typingHelp: The keyboard clatter agents make while working.
sound.notifyHelp: The ding on alerts and the session start/end effects.
sound.attentionHoldHelp: Holds a question alert this long; if the agent keeps working in the meantime (auto-approve and such), no alert is raised. 0 alerts immediately.

system.gitStatusHelp: Looks up each file's git change state (modified, added, deleted…) in "Browse work folder" and shows it as a badge. Turn it off if huge repos feel slow.
system.workdirShowIgnoredHelp: Includes .gitignore'd files and hidden (dot) files in the "Browse work folder" list. With big build outputs (node_modules, target…) the list may hit the 5000-item cap and get truncated. The .git/ directory stays excluded either way.
system.keepAwakeHelp: Keeps the computer from sleeping on its own while a character works. The display may still turn off, and closing the lid or sleeping by hand is not blocked. (macOS, Windows)
system.sessionLogHelp: Records what passed through the terminal (AI turns, commands, output) to a readable text file. Open it from a character tab's right-click "View session log" and turn it into study notes. Logs older than 30 days, or beyond 2GB total, are deleted oldest-first.
system.runRecipesHelp: Adds a Run… menu to character tabs for discovering project development, test and build commands and running them as separate processes without touching the agent terminal. Off by default.
system.mascotHelp: Floats the currently active character in a small always-on-top window separate from the app. Alerts show up there; clicking a connected IDE session returns to its original VS Code, while other sessions open the character's terminal.
system.mascotSpeechHelp: Briefly shows what the agent says while working, and its final reply when a turn ends, trimmed into a bubble above the mascot. Tool calls are not shown. CLIs that don't report mid-turn narration (such as Codex) only show the final reply.
system.mascotLightsHelp: Shows a row of status lamps under the mascot, one per target. Off (gray) means no work, green means working, yellow means waiting for your response. In by-project mode, only folders with a session connected to this app light up.
system.mascotLightsFaceHelp: Choose what to show in each lamp's round face. Even with Portrait selected, a character without a portrait falls back to its sprite face.
system.mascotLightsLabelHelp: Choose what name to show under each status lamp. Choosing Task widens the lamps. A lamp with nothing to show for the chosen option (e.g. an agent with no task info) falls back to the default name.
system.usageFloatHelp: Shows a translucent usage panel in the bottom-right when the terminal fills the whole app window. When off, usage is only shown in the bottom bar.
system.sessionCostHelp: Shows the current session's cumulative tokens and an estimated cost (based on public API rates) on the right side of the bar above the terminal. This is an estimate, not your actual subscription bill.
system.externalTerminalHelp: The app used by a terminal tab's right-click "Open in OS terminal". macOS only — ignored elsewhere.
system.externalEditorHelp: The app used to open the .txt from a terminal tab's right-click "View shell output in editor" (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+E).
system.fileIndexHelp: Everything (es.exe) is Windows-only and limited to the docs (md) palette; on failure the default scanner is used automatically.
system.terminalThemeHelp: Pins only the terminal colors to a separate palette. On the default (follow theme) the terminal changes with the app theme.
system.opencodeKeyHelp: Shows your OpenCode Go subscription's 5h, weekly and monthly usage in the bottom usage badge and details (or set the OPENCODE_API_KEY environment variable). Once saved it stays in the app and is never shown again.

control.title: CLI control (external)
control.help: Opens a local (127.0.0.1) control server so agent-office ctl … or a script can drive this app. Even when on, commands run only after you approve explicitly below (two steps). It is a security surface, so it is off by default.
control.usageIntro: Inside a session terminal you can use it right away:
control.autoRunHelp: Lets the approved CLI start, resume, pause and end plan auto-runs and type into sessions with ctl ask. Reading status and handing over to a person (autorun status, escalate) work without this. The CLI cannot continue a run a person paused.

firstRun.title: Welcome to Agent Office
firstRun.intro: The Claude Code / Codex / Pi / Kilo / Antigravity integrations are optional. You can start with them off and turn them on any time from ⚙ in the bottom bar.

modelPicker.failed: Could not load the list — you can type a model id yourself.
modelPicker.empty: No matching model — you can use it as typed.

shortcuts.help: Open an agent's terminal with a key. Works only while the app window is focused. Click a field, then press the keys to record them; Esc cancels. Dimmed text is the suggested key and is saved only when you click Suggested.
shortcuts.notifyHelp: Opens the terminal of the agent with the oldest pending notification. Opening it clears that notification, so pressing again moves to the next one.
shortcuts.clockedOut: Clocked out — the shortcut does nothing until the agent is back.

problem.needsModifier: Include at least one of Ctrl, Alt or ⌘.
problem.terminalKey: Shells and TUIs in the terminal use this key. Use ⌘ or Ctrl+Alt.
problem.reserved: The app or the OS already uses this key.

webDash.title: Web dashboard (tailnet / LAN browser)
webDash.help: While the app runs, serve a small web page so a phone or another computer can see character status and agent conversation logs. Conversations are read-only; you can only send indirect commands such as restarting a terminal, interrupting, running Claude/Codex, sending tasks and discussions. The address carries an access token.
webDash.rotateHelp: If an address leaked, make a new token. Connected devices are dropped and must open the new address.
webDash.imagesHelp: Show images from agent conversations (pasted pictures, image files the agent read) as thumbnails in the web conversation log.

errors.web-dash-no-network: No address found on the chosen network, so it is open on this computer (127.0.0.1) only. Check that Tailscale is on or that you are on a LAN. It attaches automatically when an address appears.
errors.web-dash-bind-failed: Could not open the port. If another program uses it, pick another port.
errors.web-dash-tailscale-missing: The tailscale command was not found, so the tailnet address is served over HTTP. Install the Tailscale CLI to use HTTPS.
errors.web-dash-https-not-enabled: HTTPS certificates are off for this tailnet, so it is served over HTTP. Turn on MagicDNS and HTTPS Certificates in the Tailscale admin console (DNS); it switches to HTTPS within 10 minutes.
errors.web-dash-https-failed: Could not get a Tailscale certificate, so the tailnet address is served over HTTP. It retries in 10 minutes.

webDash.lanTls: LAN addresses use HTTPS with a certificate made by this computer. Browsers warn the first time: check that the CA's SHA-256 fingerprint in the certificate details matches the one below, then continue. To skip the warning, open /ca.crt after the LAN address on that device and install the CA certificate (on iOS, then turn it on in Settings › General › About › Certificate Trust Settings).

shellAssist.intro: Tell a shell character (turn it on in Profile › Terminal) what you want, and the LLM set here makes one command for it. They are tried top to bottom; one that is off or not answering is skipped. When a command finishes, the same LLM explains the result in a sentence or two.
shellAssist.examples: Any OpenAI-compatible address works. E.g. Ollama http://localhost:11434 · LM Studio http://localhost:1234/v1 · another PC (e.g. a 4090 Windows box) by its tailnet address http://<pc>.<tailnet>.ts.net:11434 (start Ollama with OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0 to accept outside connections). Making one command is easy work; a 14B coder model is plenty.
shellAssist.label: Name
shellAssist.modelHelp: A model loaded on that server. Press Check connection to pick from its list.
shellAssist.apiKeyHelp: Most local servers need none. If set, it is sent as Bearer.
shellAssist.probeEmpty: Connected, but the model list is empty.
shellAssist.modelMissing: The model you entered is not in the list.
shellAssist.explainHelp: Explains the output in a sentence or two after each command. Commands with no output skip the LLM.
shellAssist.fallback: Fall back to the cloud when local fails
shellAssist.fallbackHelp: If every local LLM fails, try again with the provider below. The request and recent command output then go to the cloud.
shellAssist.fallbackModelHelp: Leave empty for that provider's default label-summary model.
shellAssist.openrouterKey: Set the OpenRouter key in the summarizer settings on the General tab.
shellAssist.profileHint: After turning a shell character on or off, restart that character's terminal to start recording commands.

link.title: Machine link (tailnet / LAN)
link.help: Connect Agent Office on other computers in the same tailnet or LAN as host and clients. One host owns the task board and orchestration; a client attaches to a single host. There is no discovery — enter the host address yourself.

modeHelp.host: Other computers attach to this one. A host can't attach to another host.
modeHelp.client: This computer attaches to one host.

link.version: Link protocol v{{protocol}} · app {{app}} — both computers need the same protocol version.

host.needsWebDash: Clients connect through this computer's web dashboard server. Turn on the web dashboard in the Control tab.
host.addresses: Address to enter on the client:
host.codeIntro: Enter this code on the client:

client.addressHelp: Enter the address shown in the host's Settings › Machines (e.g. https://192.168.0.5:7788). For LAN addresses the host certificate is pinned at pairing so later connections can check it is the same host.
client.forgetHelp: Forgetting here leaves this device in the host's list. Unpair it on the host too.
client.updateThis: The host (v{{host}}) speaks a different link protocol and refused the connection. Update Agent Office on this computer (v{{mine}}).
client.updateHost: The host (v{{host}}) speaks a different link protocol and refused the connection. Update Agent Office on the host (this computer is v{{mine}}).

errors.link-address-invalid: Couldn't read the host address. Example: https://192.168.0.5:7788
errors.link-address-insecure: LAN addresses need HTTPS (plain http only for this computer and tailnet IPs).
errors.link-not-host: The other computer isn't in host mode.
errors.link-not-client: Pairing is only available in client mode.
errors.link-pair-code-invalid: Wrong code. After several wrong tries the host discards the code.
errors.link-pair-no-code: The host has no valid code. Create a new code on the host.
errors.link-pair-host-unverified: The other side couldn't prove the code. Check that the address is the right host.
errors.link-self: This computer can't attach to itself.
errors.link-tls-pin-mismatch: The host certificate isn't the expected one. Someone may be in the middle, so pairing stopped.
errors.link-tls-failed: Couldn't verify the host certificate. On a tailnet, use the .ts.net name instead of the IP.
errors.link-tls-not-pinned: No pinned certificate for this address. Pair again using this address.
errors.link-host-off: The host turned host mode off or isn't accepting links.
errors.link-unauthorized: The host unpaired this device. Pair again.
errors.link-protocol-mismatch: Different link protocol versions; the connection was refused. Update the older app.
errors.link-host-changed: The host at this address isn't the one you paired with. Pair again.
errors.link-handshake-failed: Couldn't finish the handshake with the host.
